strategies.overview: With its outstanding power, good Speed, and variety of coverage and utility moves, Ogerpon-W is one of OU's premier physical attackers. The high power of Ivy Cudgel and Power Whip, the option to trade the latter with Trailblaze to outspeed otherwise faster foes such as Dragapult and Deoxys-S, and the option for coverage in Play Rough to nail Dragon-types such as Kyurem and Raging Bolt come together alongside Swords Dance to make Ogerpon-W a potent wallbreaker. In addition, utility attacks such as Knock Off to cripple checks like Pecharunt, Zapdos, and Dragonite, as well as U-turn to pivot on predicted switches and bring teammates in safely, means that Ogerpon-W can also run an all-out attacker set rather effectively. Moves such as Spikes, Taunt, and Encore allow it to act as a utility Pokemon able to further support its teammates beyond attacking, making the most out of the many switches it forces to progress the game. Moreover, the defensive utility granted by Water Absorb lets Ogerpon-W get on the field safely against the likes of Walking Wake and, more importantly, Alomomola and Dondozo. After Terastallization, the additional Special Defense boost also lets it take on special attackers that may otherwise pressure it, such as Iron Moth and Tornadus-T. However, Dragon- and Grass-types such as Raging Bolt, Kyurem, Hydrapple, and Sinistcha, as well as Pecharunt, can prove hard for Ogerpon-W to make progress against if it is not running the adequate coverage. Despite its good Speed, Ogerpon-W is still outsped and threatened by the likes of Tornadus-T, Dragapult, and Zamazenta. Being locked into Tera Water means that it lacks the surprise factor and set variability that other top-tier Pokemon such as Dragonite and Kingambit possess. This also applies to the fact that Ogerpon-W is locked into Wellspring Mask; particularly, Ogerpon-W does not have the option to run Heavy-Duty Boots, so it is often necessitated to be run on highly offensive teams that can forgo use of entry hazard removal or alongside partners that can provide it such as Great Tusk, Iron Treads, and Cinderace.
strategies.comments:
Other Options

Swords Dance sets may use Grassy Glide alongside Rillaboom, granting Ogerpon-W with the opportunity to get the jump on and threaten to OHKO Pokemon that would otherwise revenge kill it in Darkrai and Deoxys-S after a Swords Dance boost while also letting it revenge kill weakened foes such as Speed Booster Energy Walking Wake and Great Tusk. Substitute is another option on Swords Dance sets, allowing Ogerpon-W to absorb Garganacl's Salt Cure while blocking status moves such as Galarian Weezing's Will-O-Wisp and Toxapex's Toxic similar to Taunt, and it is preferred to be run alongside Horn Leech to offset the HP loss. Ogerpon-W may opt to run bulky EV spreads alongside Synthesis on its Swords Dance and Utility sets, such as investing 252 EVs in HP to make it a sturdier check against the likes of Ting-Lu, Great Tusk, and Iron Treads; in particular the investment allows it to avoid OHKOs from the likes of Choice Specs Dragapult's Draco Meteor, Life Orb Zamazenta's Close Combat, and +2 Gholdengo's Shadow Ball. All-out attacker variants may drop one of its attacks for a utility move such as Taunt or Encore, getting the most out of Ogerpon-W's coverage while still providing support for its teammates. Spiky Shield may be used to scout attacks from Choice item users such as Dragapult, Walking Wake, and Darkrai, stop revenge killing attempts from Lokix and Slither Wing's First Impression, and chip at physical attackers to put them in range of Ogerpon-W's attack. Low Kick and Superpower may be considered to OHKO Kingambit, as well as Kyurem after a round of Stealth Rock, with Superpower making up for its drops by also netting an OHKO against Darkrai. Finally, Wood Hammer may be run over Power Whip due to its accuracy.

movesets.name: Utility
movesets.description:
Ogerpon-W can function as an excellent utility piece on balance and bulky offensive teams, primarily those based around hazard stacking. This is courtesy of it being one of the best offensive Spikers in the metagame, as it forces switches consistently by threatening common Pokemon like Great Tusk, Ting-Lu, and Landorus-T. U-turn enables Ogerpon-W to gain momentum on usual switch-ins like Dragonite, Kyurem, and Hydrapple while also giving it a super effective move against opposing Ogerpon formes and Hisuian Samurott. Knock Off can be used to cripple defensive cores that are reliant on Heavy-Duty Boots like Pecharunt, Alomomola, and Sinsitcha while also hitting Dragapult and Galarian Slowking super effectively. Spikes helps apply constant pressure against a variety of playstyles, especially when used in combination with Knock Off. Synthesis provides some much-needed longevity to Ogerpon-W, considering it is a hazard-weak pokemon itself while also enabling it to switch in multiple times on moves like Ting-Lu's Ruination and Great Tusk's Headlong Rush. Encore and Taunt are alternatives that compromise on longevity but help improve other matchups. Encore helps against setup sweepers like Swords Dance Gliscor, Calm Mind Raging Bolt, and Swords Dance Kingambit. Taunt is useful in preventing hazards from going up, improves matchups against more defensively oriented teams by preventing recovery moves like Roost on Corviknight and Rest on Dondozo, denies hazard removal through Defog, and prevents status moves like Toxic from Gliscor and Will-O-Wisp from Galarian Weezing. Dropping U-turn in place of Knock Off can be considered in cases where the team lacks ways to remove Heavy-Duty Boots. An alternative spread of 8 HP / 12 Def / 236 Atk / 252 Spe permits Ogerpon-W to survive a Power Whip from full from opposing Ogerpon formes and a Close Combat from maximum Attack Iron Valiant and Great Tusk after Stealth Rock. A well-timed Terastallization can also turn this set from a utility Spiker to a potent wallbreaker in the right matchup, securing crucial 2HKOs with Ivy Cudgel on Pokemon like Zapdos while also removing its weakness to moves like Iron Moth's Sludge Wave and Corviknight's Brave Bird.

Utility Ogerpon-W functions best on entry hazard-stacking structures that aim to get hazards up quickly and pressure multiple switches through offensive momentum. Stealth Rock users like Great Tusk, Ting-Lu, and Garganacl partner well with Ogerpon-W to form a hazard-stacking duo. Garganacl in particular synergizes well with Ogerpon-W, as it handles problematic Pokemon like Zapdos, Dragapult, and Pecharunt. Other Spikers like Hisuian Samurott and Skarmory also complement Ogerpon-W well in cases where it opts not to run Spikes. This set becomes doubly effective when used in conjunction with another Knock Off user in order to maximize the pressure mounted by hazards. Pokemon like Darkrai, Iron Treads, and Gliscor are excellent teammates in this regard. Iron Treads helps keep hazards off, serves as a secondary Knock Off user, and matches up well against Pokemon like Raging Bolt and Dragonite that like to come in on Ogerpon-W. In return, Ogerpon-W helps against Ground- and Fire-types that Iron Treads struggles against, like Moltres, Great Tusk, and Gliscor. Moltres and Zapdos can pair well with Ogerpon-W to create a pivoting core while also helping against physical threats like Zamazenta and Cinderace, which can outspeed and threaten Ogerpon-W. They also provide the added benefit of punishing common spinners. Pecharunt can perform the role of a pivoting teammate to great effect due to Parting Shot while also acting as a spinblocker. These pivoting teammates help bring Ogerpon-W in safely, improving its longevity on sets that elect to drop Synthesis. Pokemon that struggle against Ground-types and Ting-Lu in particular, such as Raging Bolt, Gholdengo, and Iron Crown, greatly appreciate the utility provided by Ogerpon-W. Late-game cleaners like IronPress Zamazenta and Swords Dance Kingambit also make great teammates since they are often perfectly set up to win late-game by the pressure mounted through the course of the game by Ogerpon-W and hazard stacking. Due to a lack of Grass-type coverage, this set sometimes struggles to break common bulky Water-types like Primarina, Toxapex, and Tera Water Garganacl, though they can be pressured by hazards and Knock Off. Galarian Slowking and Garganacl both cover these matchups perfectly.

movesets.name: Swords Dance
movesets.description:
Ogerpon-W can utilize the explosive power boost gifted to it by Swords Dance to become truly unwallable, with its primary STAB combination lacking proper answers. Acting as an absurdly powerful wallbreaker, Ogerpon-W’s is able to keep many walls in check due to its sheer power, as it can easily take advantage of the passive nature of most of these walls, including the likes of Alomomola, Dondozo, and Ting-Lu, to freely set up with Swords Dance. Ogerpon-W is notably also one of the few physical attackers that doesn’t mind Moltres. It also acts as one of the few checks for Gliscor in the tier, being able to exploit Gliscor’s tendency to spam Protect to set up. On paper, regular Dragon-types may come in as checks; however, Ogerpon-W has properly adapted its arsenal for them by using Play Rough to hit foes like Dragonite and Walking Wake. Ogerpon-W may also run the uncommon but sweep-starting Trailblaze to get the jump on otherwise faster Pokemon such as Dragapult, Darkrai, Zamazenta, and some Choice Scarf users like Enamorus and Gholdengo. It is also commonly found wielding Knock Off to remove Heavy-Duty Boots from foes such as Zapdos, Pecharunt, Dragonite, and Kyurem, as well to threaten Ghost-types like Dragapult, Sinistcha, and Gholdengo. Synthesis may also be used to gain a consistent form of recovery and to utilize Ogerpon-W’s nature to frequently force switches. Encore isn’t common, though is usable, being able to take full advantage of passive walls to set up Swords Dance and threaten absurd damage while also punishing Kingambit’s Sucker Punch or Raging Bolt’s Thunderclap. Horn Leech is also notable: it’s not as powerful as Power Whip but does provide a form of longevity outside of Synthesis.

Despite the fact that Ogerpon-W is locked into Tera Water, it still makes incredible use of it by making quick work of everything that doesn’t resist Ivy Cudgel, and even at that, many Water-resistant foes still struggle to tank it. Notably, +2 Attack Tera Water Ivy Cudgel always OHKOs Pokemon like Zapdos. The Special Defense boost warranted by Embody Aspect also helps in handling some Darkrai sets and special attacking Iron Valiant while also being able to take one Freeze-Dry from even Choice Specs Kyurem. Shedding its Grass typing also allows Ogerpon-W to take Sludge Wave from Iron Moth and Sludge Bomb from the likes of Galarian Slowking and Darkrai more comfortably. An Adamant nature is still very much usable: while Ogerpon-W losing out on a good chunk of its Speed for more power usually isn’t ideal, it’s definitely noteworthy. For example, +2 Attack Adamant Tera Water Ivy Cudgel always OHKOs Galarian Weezing, which otherwise may come off as a problem for it being able to burn Ogerpon-W while also OHKOing Corviknight after rocks. However, the Speed drop is noticeable, as Ogerpon-W is no longer able to outspeed Pokemon like Enamorous, Iron Crown, and Iron Treads.

Ogerpon-W finds itself commonly used on hyper offense, bulky offense, and sometimes even balance-oriented playstyles. On most teams, it has great synergy with special attacking Iron Valiant and Raging Bolt: it deals with special walls like Clodsire and Blissey that might trouble them, as well as Assault Vest Alomomola in the case of Iron Valiant. Iron Valiant, in turn, deals with Pokemon that can outspeed and revenge kill Ogerpon-W for it like Zamazenta, Choice Band Weavile, and Darkrai, while Raging Bolt returns the favor by dealing with Zapdos. Common Pokemon used as cleaners, such as Enamorous and Darkrai, also highly appreciate Ogerpon-W's presence, as it’s able to enable them for late-game cleaning. If Swords Dance hasn’t already ended the game, Ogerpon-W itself is often used as a late-game cleaner. Swords Dance also allows it to efficiently cover for teams with poor stall matchups, often on its own, by applying great pressure due to its positive matchup against common Pokemon such as Gliscor, Dondozo, and Blissey. Ogerpon-W also appreciates hazards being up on the opponent’s side, so Pokemon like Hisuian Samurott, Ting-Lu, and Deoxys-S help it out by letting Ogerpon-W OHKO Kingambit with a +2 Attack Ivy Cudgel after 1 layer of Spikes or OHKO Raging Bolt with a +2 Play Rough.

Ogerpon-W itself doesn’t have many direct counters; however, particular Pokemon like Kyurem can take an unboosted Play Rough and OHKO a non-Terastallized Ogerpon-W with Freeze-Dry. Because of this, Ogerpon-W likes having partners like Galarian Slowking and Tinkaton that can chip Kyurem down a little while being able to take a few hits from it. Galarian Slowking can provide safe pivots, while Tinkaton can set up Stealth Rock and threaten massive damage onto Kyurem with Gigaton Hammer. In return, Ogerpon-W helps by dealing with problematic Ground-types like Ting-Lu, Great Tusk, Gliscor, and Iron Treads. Raging Bolt may be a nuisance against Ogerpon-W lacking Play Rough, so once again, Great Tusk comes in as a great partner. Likewise, Dragonite is quite troublesome for Ogerpon-W lacking Play Rough: if Dragonite is running an unfavorable Tera type, then teammates like Zapdos are quite helpful. Ogerpon-W, when paired with Zamazenta and Dragonite, overwhelm shared checks like Pecharunt, Zapdos, and Galarian Weezing. Amoongus notably has a niche in OU for being able to wall Ogerpon-W effectively, so partners like Moltres, Kyurem, and Gholdengo lend a hand in breaking it. Pecharunt can also wall Ogerpon-W, as it can reliably stomach hits from even +2 Attack Ivy Cudgel, paired with the presence of Sinistcha also being unignorable by Ogerpon-W, partners such as Gholdengo, Darkrai, and Kingambit show themselves to be very beneficial. Dragapult can easily burn Ogerpon-W or chip it down with U-turn; though Kingambit also hates being burnt, it still very much helps against Dragapult. Ogerpon-W returns the favor by removing Kingambit’s checks like Dondozo, Great Tusk, and Moltres. Ogerpon-W by no means is bulky; thus, it highly appreciates being able to be safely brought onto the field, so partners like Galarian Slowking, Landorus-T, and Cinderace are extremely useful, with Ogerpon-W being able to threaten Pokemon that threaten them like Great Tusk or Gliscor. Ogerpon-W generally prospers in the absence of entry hazards, as it’s vulnerable to chip damage. Hazard removers such as Great Tusk really come in handy here, for which Ogerpon-W in turn helps by dealing with bulky Water-types like Alomomola and Dondozo.

movesets.name: All-Out Attacker
movesets.description:
Running four attacking moves gives Ogerpon-W excellent coverage against any opponent. Power Whip is Ogerpon-W's strongest Grass-type move, but Horn Leech gives Ogerpon-W some recovery in exchange for power. In addition to its superb STAB moves, Ogerpon-W runs Play Rough for Dragon-types such as Dragonite, Kyurem, Raging Bolt, and Hydrapple. Knock Off provides the team with a utility option to remove Heavy-Duty Boots from common users like Zapdos, Pecharunt, Dragonite, and Sinistcha, preventing them from switching in for free, as well as still targeting Dragapult. Trailblaze can be used to give it a solid late-game cleaning potential, letting it outspeed would-be revenge killers like Dragapult, Darkrai, and Choice Scarf Gholdengo after a boost. U-turn is an alternative that gives Ogerpon-W the ability to pivot out of bad matchups at the cost of potential coverage. Ogerpon-W benefits from running either a Jolly or Adamant nature: Jolly allows it to outspeed Walking Wake, Iron Crown, Enamorus, Iron Treads, and Keldeo, whereas Adamant can be used for more power, and is the preferred nature if running Trailblaze to help compensate for the Speed drop. Ogerpon-W is locked to Tera Water, which allows it to guarantee OHKOs with Ivy Cudgel against Darkrai and Iron Valiant. Tera Water also removes Ogerpon-W’s weakness to U-Turn and increases its survivability against foes like Iron Moth and Gholdengo thanks to Embody Aspect.

Ogerpon-W is an excellent addition to offense teams and supports them as a premier wallbreaker and revenge killer. Powerful offensive teammates like Dragonite and Kingambit form strong cores that can break down opposing structures: Dragonite can assist Ogerpon-W in pressuring foes like Pecharunt and Zapdos, while Kingambit checks Dragapult. Ogerpon-W returns the favor by threatening the likes of Great Tusk, Landorus-T, Moltres, and Dondozo. Ogerpon-W benefits from teammates that can set up entry hazards and keep them in place; hazards make it easier for its offensive output to break teams, and in return it can use Knock Off to remove Heavy-Duty Boots to rack up hazard damage. Great Tusk is a strong option that can set Stealth Rock as well as keep pressure on foes like Raging Bolt and Dragonite. Gholdengo can help block Rapid Spin and Defog while slowing enemies down with Thunder Wave, giving Ogerpon-W more opportunities to deal damage. Lastly, Ting-Lu can help check Raging Bolt, Pecharunt, and Dragapult. Dragapult is also a great teammate that helps Ogerpon-W by spreading paralysis to help it outspeed foes, using U-turn to pivot it in safely. Ogerpon-W in turn threatens Garganacl, Ting-Lu, Primarina, and Assault Vest Alomomola, all of which give Dragapult trouble. Raging Bolt is another option that can pick off foes weakened by Ogerpon-W with priority Thunderclap; Ogerpon-W complements Raging Bolt by dealing with threats like Great Tusk, Ting-Lu, and Iron Treads. Together, Ogerpon-W, Dragapult, and Raging Bolt can form VoltTurn pivot cores to keep strong momentum between them. Ogerpon-W is relatively frail and susceptible to taking hits from opposing offensive Pokemon like Dragonite and Iron Valiant as well as entry hazards due to lack of Heavy-Duty Boots. Defensive teammates like Zamazenta can help cover Dragonite, taking little damage from its attacks and stopping it from boosting with Dragon Dance by using Roar. Garganacl is another solid defensive teammate that can handle attacks from foes like Pecharunt, Dragapult, and Zapdos, wearing them down with Stealth Rock and Salt Cure. Ogerpon-W struggles to break through certain defensive walls like Zamazenta and Pecharunt; having powerful teammates like Iron Valiant or the aforementioned Dragapult for the former along with Darkrai or Galarian Slowking for the latter can help take care of said walls as well as keep up offensive pressure throughout the game.

strategies.comments:
Other Options

Water

Superpower is a niche move that destroys the Steel matchup after a Swords Dance.

movesets.name: Swords Dance (Water)
movesets.description:
Ogerpon-W boasts a great Attack stat complemented by an amazing Speed stat, which lets it outspeed a great number of foes such as Landorus, Hydreigon, and Keldeo, allowing it to serve as a setup sweeper on both rain and rainless Water teams. Ivy Cudgel dismantles foes such as offensive Gholdengo, Zapdos, and Galarian Slowking after a Swords Dance. Horn Leech threatens enemies such as Primarina and Keldeo. Power Whip can be used in place of Horn Leech for more power over accuracy, allowing Ogerpon-W to clean up walls such as Toxapex, Clodsire, Ting-Lu, and Hatterene after a Swords Dance. Play Rough threatens Dragon-types such as Dragonite and Kommo-o, which resist both of Ogerpon-W's STAB moves. Alternatively, Knock Off removes items such as Leftovers from annoying foes like Archaludon and Corviknight while also threatening Brambleghast. Trailblaze is another option to boost Ogerpon-W's Speed, allowing it to out wipe out Rock, Ground, and Fire teams on its own.

Swampert provides an immunity to Electric-type attacks, sets entry hazards for the team, and possesses a slow pivot option via Flip Turn, allowing Ogerpon-W to safely come on a weakened threat to set up. Hisuian Samurott is another partner that provides hazard support via Ceaseless Edge. It also checks fast foes like Dragapult and chipped Choice Specs Flutter Mane with Sucker Punch as well as annoying foes such as Archaludon with Sacred Sword. Greninja forms an offensive core with Ogerpon-W, serving as the special attacker of the team and helping in removing Dragonite and Ogerpon-H. Primarina is another setup sweeper that finds success in disrupting Dragon-types such as Roaring Moon and Archaludon with Draining Kiss. Toxapex is an excellent wall to deal with foes like Kleavor and Meowscarada. Toxapex spreads poison with Toxic or Toxic Spikes to wear down Iron Hands and Sinistcha, allowing Ogerpon-W to clean them up with ease. When slotted on rain teams, Ogerpon-W enjoys Pelipper's ability to set up rain and easily pivot in it using U-turn against Hisuian Samurott. Rain allows Ogerpon-W's Ivy Cudgel to OHKO foes such as Ting-Lu and Alolan Muk after Stealth Rock damage. In rain, Barraskewda breaks through Ogerpon-W's checks such as Sneasler and Tornadus-T. Empoleon provides a switch-in against special attacks from foes like Articuno and Kyurem and threatens them back. It also punishes attempts to Defog with Competitive and provides utility with Stealth Rock, Flip Turn, and Roar. Gastrodon is another defensive ally of Ogerpon-W that can be annoying to remove due to its bulk and access to Recover. It can set up hazards such as Spikes and Stealth Rock as well as disrupt foes like Gliscor and Gholdengo with Earth Power and Ice Beam.

movesets.name: Bulky Attacker
movesets.description:
• Ivy Cudgel is a strong STAB option that hits common threats like Landorus, Incineroar, and Diancie super effectively and threatens an OHKO on Flutter Mane while also dealing solid damage to neutral targets.
  • Ogerpon-W has quite a few options for its Grass-type STAB attack to hit Water-resistant foes like Palafin, Volcanion, and opposing Ogerpon-W. Horn Leech has respectable power in addition to giving Ogerpon-W a way to sustain itself, which can be helpful considering how crucial its health is. Power Whip is a stronger option, allowing Ogerpon-W to hit some targets harder than it would with Ivy Cudgel such as Tyranitar and Ursaluna.
  • Follow Me leverages Ogerpon-W's good typing to support its team and shield its teammates from threatening attacks and status moves, with Water Absorb allowing it to heal from Water-type attacks such as Palafin's Jet Punch and Volcanion's Steam Eruption. Encore punishes Fake Out, Protect, and speed control moves, forcing the Encore target to switch out or repeatedly use a detrimental move, generating momentum for Ogerpon-W's team.
  • Ogerpon-W usually uses Spiky Shield, but on faster-paced teams, it might opt to drop this for Encore due to the utility of Follow Me being desired in addition to Encore's potential to swing the momentum of a game.
  • In addition to the usual benefits, Ogerpon-W gains +1 Special Defense upon Terastallizing, considerably improving its matchups against Flutter Mane and Deoxys-A.
  • The given EV spread lets Ogerpon-W outspeed Landorus and survive a Tera Stellar Chien-Pao Icicle Crash, with the rest of the EVs going into Attack to allow Power Whip to OHKO maximum HP Flutter Mane. Alternatively, an EV spread of 252 HP / 28 Atk / 84 Def / 72 SpD / 72 Spe with an Adamant nature can be used to survive a Choice Band Tera Normal Extreme Speed from Dragonite with Sword of Ruin active or a Choice Specs Tera Fairy Moonblast from maximum Special Attack Flutter Mane while still outspeeding Smeargle and Modest Glimmora.
  • Tornadus makes a great partner for Ogerpon-W, as it provides Prankster Tailwind support and threatens Grass-types Ogerpon-W can't touch such as Rillaboom and opposing Ogerpon-W with Bleakwind Storm, and it can even strengthen Ivy Cudgel with Rain Dance. Flutter Mane threatens out Dragon-types like Baxcalibur and Raging Bolt that resist Ogerpon-W's STAB combination, and it appreciates the potential Follow Me support Ogerpon-W provides to draw strong priority attacks like Kingambit's Sucker Punch and Rillaboom's Grassy Glide away from it. Setup Pokemon such as Swords Dance Kingambit appreciate Ogerpon-W providing both Follow Me and Encore support to generate setup opportunities for them by either redirecting attacks or shutting down an opposing Pokemon.

movesets.name: Swords Dance
movesets.description:
• This set's write-up has not started yet, but here's some basic info to get you started!

  • 4 HP / 196 Atk / 52 Def / 4 SpD / 252 Spe with Jolly: This spread lets Embody Aspect Ogerpon-W survive both Choice Specs Flutter Mane's Tera Fairy Moonblast and Adamant Ogerpon-H's +1 Tera Fire Ivy Cudgel after Stealth Rock damage.

  • 156 HP / 156 Atk / 4 Def / 12 SpD / 180 Spe with Adamant: This spread lets Embody Aspect Ogerpon-W survive Tera Normal Silk Scarf Ursaluna-B's Blood Moon. It also outspeeds Modest Chi-Yu and survives Adamant Urshifu's Close Combat after Stealth Rock damage.

movesets.name: Specially Defensive
movesets.description:
• Ogerpon-W's great support movepool and Embody Aspect's Special Defense boost give it the opportunity to face premier special attackers such as Flutter Mane, Ursaluna-B, and Gholdengo head-on.

  • Horn Leech: Horn Leech's recovery can help maintain Ogerpon-W's defensive profile without compromising its offenses.

  • Substitute: Substitute has great synergy alongside Ogerpon-W's other support moves, especially Leech Seed. It's also useful for blocking status moves from foes like Ursaluna-B and Archaludon.

  • Leech Seed versus Synthesis: Due to being forced to run Wellspring Mask, Ogerpon-W misses passive recovery from items such as Leftovers, making Leech Seed a solid option for recovery. Synthesis is a more reliable recovery option at the cost of making Ogerpon-W more vulnerable to Archaludon.

  • Encore: Locking targets into an undesirable move can discourage setup attempts and passive play and allow opportunities for healing.

EV Spreads

  • 252 HP / 4 Atk / 4 Def / 188 SpD / 60 Spe with Careful: This spread aims to maximize Ogerpon-W's special bulk, and it outspeeds Modest Gholdengo, positive Speed-natured base 70 Speed foes such as Jolly Breloom, and neutral-natured base 85 Speed foes such as Rillaboom.

  • 236 HP / 4 Atk / 52 Def / 156 SpD / 60 Spe with Careful: If using Substitute and Leech Seed, this spread sacrifices some special bulk in exchange for letting Substitute withstand Archaludon's Dragon Tail.

Embody Aspect

Ogerpon-W is locked into a Water Tera type. When it Terastallizes, Water Absorb becomes Embody Aspect. This forme's Embody Aspect boosts Special Defense, making it essentially like an Assault Vest without the downsides, which can be key to taking strong hits such as those from Choice Specs Tera Fairy Flutter Mane and Tera Normal Ursaluna-B.

strategies.overview:
• Ogerpon-W has a very well-rounded stat spread, a solid typing, and an amazing movepool with great STAB moves, Spiky Shield, and Follow Me which helps it support frailer teammates.

  • A great example of a less-bulky teammate is Flutter Mane; Ogerpon-W's ability to redirect moves away from Flutter Mane can help it break through the opposing team with its strong Tera Fairy Dazzling Gleam in just a few turns.

  • Another great partner for Ogerpon-W is Kingambit, as it discourages Intimidate, which is one of the few ways to slow down Ogerpon-W's offensive capabilities, and Kingambit can even run a Swords Dance set to set-up with Follow Me support from Ogerpon-W.

  • Ogerpon-W is also already a big threat on its own, as it pressures top threats such as Landorus, Incineroar, Flutter Mane, and Urshifu-R, being especially dangerous with Tera. Ogerpon-W does struggle against Rillaboom and Raging Bolt, which resist both STAB types and can hit it super effectively after Tera.

movesets.name: Offensive Redirector
movesets.description:
• Horn Leech is the Grass-type move of choice, as Ogerpon-W appreciates the extra longevity, which becomes especially notable when combined with the Special Defense boost provided by Terastallizing.

  • The EV spread outspeeds Modest Landorus, OHKOes bulky Flutter Mane after Tera, and survives Rillaboom's Terrain-boosted Wood Hammer.

movesets.name: Offensive Redirector
movesets.description:
Ogerpon-W is often used to redirect attacks and threaten common Fire-types such as Incineroar and Chi-Yu and Ground-types such as Ursaluna-B and Landorus with Ivy Cudgel. Ogerpon-W has excellent matchups into Urshifu-R and Kyogre, both of which struggle to deal significant damage to Ogerpon-W while it can threaten them with Horn Leech or Wood Hammer. Horn Leech is used to deal consistent damage while boosting Ogerpon-W's longevity, while Wood Hammer allows Ogerpon-W to OHKO Flutter Mane and Kyogre. Ogerpon-W also matches up well into Calyrex-S and Ursaluna-B after it Terastallizes, threatening to 2HKO Calyrex-S and OHKO Ursaluna-B with Tera Water Ivy Cudgel. The HP and Defense investment allows Ogerpon-W to survive Collision Course in sun from Koraidon, Wood Hammer from Assault Vest Rillaboom, and two High Horsepowers from Calyrex-I after Terastallizing, and it gives it a high chance of surviving two Behemoth Blades from Zacian-C. The HP and Special Defense investment allows Ogerpon-W to survive Astral Barrage from Tera Ghost Choice Specs Calyrex-S, Discharge from Choice Specs Miraidon, and, when Terastallized, Blood Moon from Ursaluna-B; Ogerpon-W also has a high chance of surviving Overheat from Chi-Yu. The Attack investment allows Ogerpon-W to 2HKO Incineroar after Intimidate, and the Speed investment allows Ogerpon-W to outrun Landorus.

Ogerpon-W's redirection makes it an ideal partner for Pokemon that want to set up freely and frail offensive threats that can be KOed easily such as Calm Mind Terapagos and Choice Specs Calyrex-S, respectively. Ogerpon-W survives attacks such as Collision Course from Koraidon and Close Combat from Urshifu-R, which threaten Terapagos, and can redirect Sucker Punch from Chien-Pao, which threatens Calyrex-S. Ogerpon-W also threatens checks to Calyrex-S such as Incineroar and Chi-Yu. Ogerpon-W struggles against Miraidon, Raging Bolt, and Rillaboom, all of which wall and threaten it. Calyrex-I threatens all of these, making it an ideal partner for Ogerpon-W. Ogerpon-W benefits Calyrex-I by threatening Incineroar and redirecting attacks, such as Knock Off and Will-O-Wisp, that hinder Calyrex-I. A partner Incineroar also pairs well with Ogerpon-W, with Incineroar's Intimidate and Ogerpon-W's Embody Aspect working in tandem to make Ogerpon-W difficult to remove. Ogerpon-W supports Incineroar by redirecting attacks that threaten Incineroar such as Surging Strikes from Urshifu-R and Earth Power from Ursaluna-B.

movesets.name: Swords Dance
movesets.description: Fantastic STAB coverage, a solid Speed tier, and good coverage options all make Ogerpon-W a force to be reckoned with, being able to shatter most of the tier's physical walls such as Corviknight, Gholdengo, and Mandibuzz after a Swords Dance. Power Whip packs more of a punch, letting it OHKO RegenVest Manaphy without a Swords Dance boost, while Horn Leech grants it more longevity. Knock Off lets it threaten Desolate Land users such as Iron Moth, Ceruledge, and Heatran, while Play Rough picks off Dragon-types such as Roaring Moon, Dragonite, and Latios. Trailblaze enables Ogerpon-W to act as more of a sweeper, letting it outspeed threats such as Iron Boulder, Chien-Pao, and Deoxys-S, while Spikes can be used to help chip down Hisuian Goodra and other walls for its teammates. Ogerpon-W pairs well with fast cleaners such as Iron Boulder and Choice Scarf Roaring Moon, as they appreciate its ability to pressure Fluffy users such as Corviknight and Great Tusk thanks to Ivy Cudgel not making contact. In spite of its solid speed, Ogerpon-W is still threatened by faster targets such as Chien-Pao, Choice Scarf Azelf, and Roaring Moon, making defensive pivots such as Corviknight and Swampert crucial in order to bring it in safely.

movesets.name: All-Out Attacker
movesets.description: Ogerpon-W is a threatening wallbreaker thanks to its good stats and incredible movepool, featuring high Base Power STAB moves and strong coverage options. Power Whip is the standard Grass-type STAB move of choice due to its power, but Horn Leech can be used to avoid missing and provide Ogerpon-W with healing. Knock Off can hinder switch-ins like Intimidate Corviknight and Dragonite. Play Rough stops Dragonite from being a safe switch-in, as well as surprising Roaring Moon that try to switch in with an OHKO. U-turn allows Ogerpon-W to pivot out on bad matchups like the aforementioned Intimidate Corviknight and Dragonite. Stomping Tantrum hits Water-immune foes such as Water Absorb Heatran and Desolate Land Iron Moth and Ceruledge. Primordial Sea boosts Ogerpon-W's Ivy Cudgel to absurd levels, consistently 2HKOing non-Intimidate Corviknight while also giving Ogerpon-W a Fire immunity. Sword of Ruin is an alternative option to boost the power of all of Ogerpon-W's moves, notably OHKOing physically defensive Manaphy with Power Whip. Ogerpon-W pairs well with teammates like Zamazenta and Iron Boulder that can break through non-Fluffy Corviknight. It also appreciates Stealth Rock setters like Great Tusk and Scream Tail, as they discourage Pokemon like Dragonite from switching in and help chip down defensive Pokemon. While Ogerpon-W's Speed tier is good, it can still get easily revenge killed by Pokemon like Roaring Moon, Deoxys-S, and Zamazenta, so a strong defensive core featuring teammates such as Manaphy and Corviknight is appreciated. Ogerpon-W struggles with switching in safely, so it appreciates slow pivots like the aforementioned Corviknight and Manaphy.

movesets.name: Offensive Redirector
movesets.description:
Ogerpon-W is a threatening offensive redirector, using its good stats and strong movepool to check metagame threats such as Landorus and Heatran, as well as providing a useful Water immunity to teammates. Ivy Cudgel is useful as a strong Water-type move for Ogerpon-W and a strong Grass-type move for teammates. In a pinch, Ogerpon-W can also use Ivy Cudgel on a teammate to provide a small bit of healing thanks to Water Absorb. Wood Hammer is stronger, at the cost of having recoil, while Horn Leech improves Ogerpon-W's longevity throughout a battle. Follow Me helps allies like Gholdengo and Iron Hands to set up, as well as helping Trick Room users such as Porygon2 to set it up safely. Spiky Shield is a useful option that can protect Ogerpon-W from double targets and help it stall out Trick Room, while Swords Dance synergizes well with Follow Me and can be used if other teammates are carrying Protect. The given EV spread allows it to outspeed Landorus and survive Landorus's Sludge Bomb, with the rest being put in Attack. Ogerpon-W struggles against Grass- and Dragon-types such as Rillaboom, Sinistcha, Dragonite, and Raging Bolt, as they resist Ogerpon-W's STAB combination. Intimidate users such as Incineroar and Landorus-T can also be problematic, as they dampen Ogerpon-W's damage output despite its positive type matchup into them. Ogerpon-W is forced into Tera Water, but it uniquely gives Ogerpon-W a useful Special Defense boost, helping against Pokemon like Gholdengo and Tornadus.

Notable Partners

Intimidate Answers: Pokemon that can take advantage of Intimidate like Galarian Zapdos and Kingambit or Pokemon that can block it like Dragonite make for good partners, as they can prevent Ogerpon-W's damage output from being lowered. When alongside these Intimidate answers, Ogerpon-W can utilize its good matchup into Intimidate users such as Landorus-T and Incineroar and check them properly.

Physical Attackers: Ogerpon-W is good with a lot of physical attackers such as Chien Pao, Iron Hands, and Ursaluna. Ogerpon-W can pass them Swords Dance and help them set up with Follow Me or utilize its strong offensive synergy with these teammates, such as Chien Pao beating the Grass- and Dragon-types that Ogerpon-W struggles with, Ogerpon-W beating Landorus for Iron Hands and Iron Hands beating Tornadus in return, and Ursaluna beating Dragonite for Ogerpon-W. Additionally, Chien-Pao provides Sword of Ruin, making the duo very obnoxious to switch into considering the type synergy between them, as well as making Ivy Cudgel more of a threat against Incineroar.

Water-weak Pokemon Teammates such as Heatran, Ting-Lu, Glimmora, and both Landorus formes appreciate the Water immunity that Ogerpon-W grants to its team. Follow Me can enable Substitute users like Landorus and Heatran, while Heatran can check Rillaboom, Sinistcha, and Amoonguss. Glimmora can provide entry hazard support to chip down would-be checks to Ogerpon-W, as well as check Flying-types like Tornadus and Dragonite that would otherwise cause problems.

Trick Room Setters Pokemon like Porygon2 and Diancie benefit from Ogerpon-W’s ability to redirect attacks that would otherwise threaten them, allowing them to set up Trick Room more easily. These teammates also have additional synergies, such as Porygon2 passing Download and Diancie passing Clear Body, as well as Ogerpon-W providing Diancie with a Water immunity.

strategies.overview:
Draft Order: Round 2 onwards

Price Range: 13-14 points

Tera Price Range: 18 points

Overview: Ogerpon-W functions as a strong wallbreaker and sweeper, especially as a Tera Captain. It has a good STAB combination and solid Attack stat, which can be further boosted by Swords Dance and Terastallization. It also has a good Speed tier that can be amplified with Trailblaze. It also has solid support options, such as Encore, Knock Off, Spikes and U-turn, which can make it useful in matchups where it has a hard time wallbreaking. Despite its immense power, Ogerpon-W is significantly less flexible than other high-priced Tera Captains, being unable to change its item or Tera type. In addition, bulky Grass- and Dragon-types, as well as some opposing Tera users, can be difficult to muscle past.
strategies.comments:
Common Roles

Setup Wallbreaker: Ogerpon-W excels at setting up Swords Dance and putting immediate pressure on the opposing team with its extremely powerful STAB moves. It has a good variety of coverage options like Knock Off, Play Rough, and Superpower to break past its checks. In addition, the Special Defense boost from Embody Aspect can come in handy to survive a special hit from a faster Pokemon that would ordinarily revenge kill Ogerpon-W. Depending on the matchup, Ogerpon-W can make use of utility moves such as Synthesis and Encore to give it more opportunities to setup and wallbreak.

Trailblaze Cleaner: In certain matchups where Ogerpon-W is not expected to sweep, Ogerpon-W can function as a potential late-game cleaner after using Trailblaze and using Tera-boosted Ivy Cudgel to blow past the rest of the opposing team once it is sufficiently weakened.

Entry Hazard Utility: In matchups where Ogerpon-W would find it difficult to wallbreak or sweep, it can fulfill a more supporting role of setting up Spikes to pressure the opposing team and assist team members. In conjunction with Leech Seed, Horn Leech, and Synthesis for recovery; Knock Off and Encore for disruption; and U-turn for pivoting, Ogerpon-W can always accomplish something meaningful in a given matchup.

Common Moves

Primary STAB Moves: Ivy Cudgel, Power Whip, Horn Leech, Wood Hammer

Setup Moves: Swords Dance, Trailblaze

Utility Moves: U-turn, Taunt, Encore, Substitute, Spikes, Synthesis, Brick Break

Coverage: Superpower, Low Kick, Play Rough, Knock Off, Zen Headbutt, Rock Tomb

Niche Moves

Spiky Shield: This move helps Ogerpon-W get some free damage against physical attackers, which could help it or its teammates KO the foe later on. It can also be useful in scouting Choice-locked foes to eliminate the guessing game of whether or not Ogerpon-W should Terastallize.

Quick Attack: Quick Attack can be an effective late-game option to pick off faster Pokemon that are weakened from attacks or hazards.

Common Items

Wellspring Mask: Ogerpon-W must hold this item.

Tera

Ogerpon-W is a top-tier Tera Captain, using Tera Water-boosted Ivy Cudgels to wallbreak and sweep through all but the bulkiest of drafts. In addition, Terastallization gives it an arguably better defensive typing in certain scenarios, trading its Ground resistance for losing weaknesses to Poison-, Flying-, and Bug-type moves, especially U-turn. This, in combination with the Special Defense boost it gains from Embody Aspect once Terastallized, can aid in both setting up and surviving attempts to revenge kill.

Draft Strategy

Ogerpon-W is a great option if you are looking for an excellent physical wallbreaker and sweeper. Many offensive or balance teams appreciate the role it provides. However, Ogerpon-W does a poor job at filling the defensive roles typical of Water-types and especially Grass-types due to Terastallizing often, so having those key resistances present elsewhere in the draft is important.

Special Wallbreakers: Many special attackers like Darkrai, Iron Valiant, and Landorus can compliment Ogerpon-W's physical offense when it comes to pressuring the opposing team and beating Ogerpon-W's checks.

Speed Control: While Ogerpon-W has a good Speed tier, it can get forced out fairly easily by naturally faster Pokemon or Choice Scarf users; therefore, it is to advised draft faster Pokemon alongside Ogerpon-W such as Weavile, Roaring Moon and Cinderace.

Entry Hazard Control: Ogerpon-W greatly appreciates strong entry hazard setters like Ting-Lu and Garchomp to accumulate chip damage on its checks, turning many 2HKOs for its Tera-boosted Ivy Cudgel into OHKOs. It is also advised to pair Ogerpon-W with proper hazard removal, such as Iron Treads or Terapagos, especially if you plan on making use of its strength as an offensive pivot, as it is unable to run Heavy-Duty Boots.

Checks and Counters

Grass-types and Dragon-types: Bulky Grass- and Dragon-types like Hydrapple, Zarude, and Dragonite resist Ogerpon-W's STAB combination and force it to run specific coverage over other valuable moves. Tera Grass and Tera Dragon are also both common answers to Ogerpon-W, which can be capitalized on by bringing Ice-type offense.

Faster Threats: While Ogerpon-W has an acceptable Speed tier, it is susceptible to getting revenge killed by Choice Scarf users and naturally faster Pokemon such as Meowscarada, Sneasler, and Iron Boulder. However, specially offensive Choice Scarf users require prior damage on Ogerpon-W due to the Special Defense boost gained from Embody Aspect.

Status: Being a fast physical attacker, Ogerpon-W is greatly hindered by both burns and paralysis. Chip damage from poison can also end a sweep prematurely by making it easier to revenge kill.

movesets.name: Swords Dance (HP, Atk, Def, SpD, Spe)
Offensive
movesets.description:
• Ogerpon-W is a very strong offensive threat with a wide movepool capable of adapting itself to a variety of threats in 1v1.
  • Power Whip hits opposing Water- and Ground-types like Primarina and Ursaluna. Wood Hammer may be used to not deal with Power Whip's 85% accuracy, though taking recoil may cause Ogerpon-W to lose some matchups that Power Whip would be a better fit for, such as against opposing Ogerpon-W.
  • Ivy Cudgel muscles through Fire- and Ground-types like Volcarona, Heatran, and Landorus-T.
  • Ogerpon-W's blisteringly fast base 110 Speed allows it to shut down many defensive threats that enjoy boosting their Defense stat such as Corviknight and Iron Crown by locking them into a status move with Encore.
  • Superpower may be used to secure KOs on threats that would otherwise survive Ogerpon-W's STAB attacks such as bulky Choice Specs Porygon-Z and non-Counter Hisuian Goodra.
  • U-turn can KO bulkier, slower Hoopa-U sets that would survive Ogerpon-W's other moves.
  • Knock Off can be used to outplay Custap Berry Pokemon such as Skeledirge and faster Choice Scarf users like Metagross.
  • Trailblaze lets Ogerpon-W get the jump on faster Pokemon that could potentially outplay it such as Encore + Disable Iron Valiant.
  • Spiky Shield can be used to secure OHKOs against Pokemon like Custap Berry Skeledirge and can stop Fly from Landorus-T.
  • Ogerpon-W's Speed is maximized to outspeed Alolan Ninetales and Speed tie itself in the mirror matchup. The rest of the EVs are placed to maximize its Attack.
  • Because of Ogerpon-W's immense strength, versatility, and Speed, its moveset is completely flexible and can open a myriad of options for its partners. Unfortunately, offensive Ogerpon-W can be overwhelmed by threats that can survive an attack and KO it back, such as Haxorus, so partners that help Ogerpon-W overcome this issue like Sylveon and Iron Crown are helpful.

movesets.name: Charm
movesets.description:
• Charm + Synthesis allows Ogerpon-W to outlast slower physical attackers like Haxorus and Iron Hands. Synthesis can also help defeat Draco Meteor users like Speed Booster Energy Walking Wake.
  • Ivy Cudgel is a reliable Water-type STAB move used to chip down the likes of Metagross and Skeledirge.
  • Power Whip is used primarily to take down other Water-types, most notably Primarina and Urshifu-R.
  • If some of these Pokemon are already well covered by a partner, Encore is worth considering. Encore can foil the plans of some setup Pokemon, such as Swords Dance Iron Hands, that would otherwise outlast Charm and then KO Ogerpon-W. Encore also allows for it to break through some stall Pokemon, such as Reflect + Calm Mind Cresselia.
  • 152 Speed EVs and a Jolly nature allow Ogerpon-W to outspeed Haxorus and Urshifu. The defensive investment gives the best chances to survive a Close Combat from Choice Band Urshifu, allowing Ogerpon-W to be sent in against both of its formes without having to guess at Team Preview.

movesets.name: Specially Defensive
movesets.description:
• Power Whip is for Primarina and non-Sap Sipper Azumarill and is the best option against non-positive Defense-natured Sylveon.
  • Ivy Cudgel is for non-Passho Berry Volcarona and Rhyperior.
  • Knock Off should be used against Spectrier and Porygon-Z.
  • Superpower guarantees the matchup against both Hisuian Goodra and bulkier Porygon-Z sets after Knock Off, while Encore allows Ogerpon-W to defeat Pokemon like Registeel.
  • The Speed EVs allow Ogerpon-W to outspeed non-Choice Scarf Porygon-Z, while the HP and Special Defense EVs give it the best roll to survive Hyper Beam from Modest Porygon-Z after Ogerpon-W's Knock Off.
  • If Power Whip and another move both KO an opposing Pokemon, it is best to use the other move due to accuracy.
  • Against slower Pokemon that attempt to stall out Ogerpon-W, Encore can be used to lock them into a status move.
  • Knock Off can also be used in some matchups to remove an opposing Custap Berry on the turn that Pokemon like Custap Berry Sylveon use Endure.

movesets.name: SubSeed
movesets.description:
• Maximum Speed is to outspeed everything Ogerpon-W can, including non-Choice Scarf Landorus-T and Manaphy.
  • The Defense EVs let Ogerpon-W survive Choice Band Metagross's Psychic Fangs, while the Special Defense EVs let it take Ursaluna-B's combo of Blood Moon and Vacuum Wave.
  • Ogerpon-W should use Leech Seed turn one and then alternate between Spiky Shield and Substitute until the foe is KOed or is within range of Ogerpon-W's attacks.
  • Without Spiky Shield, Ogerpon-W relies more on its offensive capabilities. After using Leech Seed, it should use Substitute until it's able to KO foes with either Power Whip or Ivy Cudgel.
  • Leech Seed and Substitute are standard for the strategy. While Spiky Shield isn't mandatory, it is usually used to increase healing from Leech Seed and to stall out the foe's HP.
  • One or two attacking moves are used; Ivy Cudgel is better for hitting Fire-, Ground-, and Rock-types like Landorus-T, Skeledirge, and Rhyperior for super effective damage and is better against IronPress sets from Pokemon like Registeel and Corviknight because of Ivy Cudgel's higher crit rate. Power Whip's main advantage is that it is better against Water-types, like Primarina and Manaphy.

movesets.name: Defensive
movesets.description:
• This Ogerpon-W takes a more defensive route thanks to its decent bulk and access to Counter in order to flip otherwise losing matchups, such as against non-Triple Axel Meowscarada.
  • Power Whip hits Water-type Pokemon such as Primarina super effectively and is Ogerpon-W's best option against neutral matchups like Sylveon.
  • Ivy Cudgel threatens Fire- and Ground-type Pokemon such as Skeledirge and Landorus-T.
  • Counter allows defensive Ogerpon-W to retaliate against physical foes that would either threaten to KO it or feel that a physical attack is their best move against offensive Ogerpon-W sets, such as non-Triple Axel Choice Band Meowscarada and opposing Ogerpon-W. Alternatively, Knock Off may be used to remove Custap Berry from Pokemon such as Skeledirge.
  • U-turn is Ogerpon-W's best option against non-defensive Hoopa-U, since it gets OHKOed. Alternatively, Encore is useful to lock down a slower foe focused on boosting their stats, such as Cresselia and defensive Iron Crown, or to outplay Endure Custap Berry sets from Pokemon such as Sylveon and Skeledirge.
  • The Speed EVs allow Ogerpon-W to outspeed Hoopa-U whereas the HP and Defense EVs give Ogerpon-W the best rolls against Adamant Choice Band Meowscarada.
  • Defensive Ogerpon-W won't have the firepower to threaten Pokemon like Fast Choice Specs Porygon-Z, Bulky Hoopa-U, and Ursaluna, so teammates that can cover this weakness such as Corviknight are appreciated.

movesets.name: Swords Dance
movesets.description:
Ogerpon-W is a very threatening wallbreaker that gets many opportunities to set up with Swords Dance, as it can threaten key defensive pieces like Landorus-T, Great Tusk, and Heatran with its STAB moves. Power Whip is the preferred option, as it OHKOes Great Tusk and Alomomola, but Horn Leech can keep Ogerpon-W healthy. Superpower hits potential switch-ins such as Ferrothorn and Archaludon. Play Rough can allow Ogerpon-W to target foes such as Dragonite, Raging Bolt, and Mega Latios, which would otherwise switch in comfortably.

Ogerpon-W tends to fit on many different playstyles from hyper offense to balance, as it is a potent wallbreaker capable of threatening defensive teams. Its Water immunity is also appreciated against rain teams. Pokemon like Great Tusk and Landorus-T value Ogerpon-W's ability to break through bulky Water-types such as Alomomola, Slowbro, and Dondozo. In return, these two provide Stealth Rock support as well as an Electric immunity that can stop revenge killing attempts from Tapu Koko and Raging Bolt. In addition, both teammates can provide entry hazard removal, which Ogerpon-W appreciates, as it is vulnerable to chip damage. Ogerpon-W struggles with threats like Raging Bolt, Mega Latios, and Mega Latias, so Pursuit trappers like Kingambit and Mega Tyranitar are welcomed. Ogerpon-W does not like taking many hits, so it appreciates U-turn from teammates such as Landorus-T and Tapu Koko to enter the field safely against Pokemon that want to come in on them such as Alomomola for the former and Ting-Lu for the latter. Non-Superpower Ogerpon-W can struggle to dent checks such as Ferrothorn and Archaludon, so Pokemon like Zamazenta and Mega Lopunny are valued to make up for the lack of coverage. Non-Play Rough Ogerpon-W should have partners that can pressure checks like Dragonite and Raging Bolt like Great Tusk and Tapu Koko.

movesets.name: Offensive Pivot
movesets.description:
Ogerpon-W is an offensive pivot that threatens common defensive Pokemon like Landorus-T, Gliscor, and Heatran. Courtesy of its ability, Ogerpon-W can answer a plethora of offensive Water-types, such as Mega Swampert and Urshifu-R, while ignoring Scald and Flip Turn from Slowbro, Toxapex, and Alomomola. Power Whip OKHOes Ursaluna and Great Tusk after minor chip damage, whereas Horn Leech provides it with longevity in exchange for power. U-turn allows Ogerpon-W to pivot out of checks such as Raging Bolt, Ferrothorn, and Dragonite. Knock Off is used to cripple switch-ins like Dragonite and Ferrothorn by removing their Heavy-Duty Boots and Leftovers, respectively. Alternatively, Encore can lock certain defensive pieces into recovery moves such as Toxapex and Mega Scizor. Encore also helps Ogerpon-W avoid mind games against priority moves from Raging Bolt and Kingambit and denies faster Pokemon like Zamazenta from setting up on it. Taunt is also an option to deny entry hazard-setting attempts from walls such as Ferrothorn and Clefable while ensuring Ogerpon-W walls Toxapex and Alomomola. Spikes can be used to wear down checks such as Ferrothorn and Raging Bolt lacking Heavy-Duty Boots, as it has the remarkable ability to force switches.

Ogerpon-W commonly fits on bulky offense and balance teams. Pokemon such as Great Tusk and Landorus-T appreciate its presence due to its ability to threaten foes such as Alomomola, Urshifu-R, and Moltres. In return, these teammates can provide entry hazard removal through Rapid Spin and Defog to prevent Ogerpon-W from being worn down quickly. Additionally, Landorus-T can bring it in with U-turn against Pokemon like Alomomola and Gliscor. Ogerpon-W is vulnerable to faster threats such as Iron Valiant and Zamazenta, so it appreciates teammates like bulky Volcarona and Landorus-T to answer Iron Valiant and check Zamazenta, respectively. Ogerpon-W also loves Spikes support from Pokemon like Mega Diancie to wear down checks such as Ferrothorn and Raging Bolt and help rack up chip damage in combination with U-turn.

movesets.name: Swords Dance (Water)
movesets.description: Ogerpon-W is a strong wallbreaker on Water teams by virtue of its great Attack, which can be further boosted by Swords Dance; great Speed; a unique resistance to Ground, improving that matchup; and a selection of coverage options it can choose from. Horn Leech not only lets Ogerpon-W recover HP, but it also targets the likes of Urshifu-R, Slowbro, and Mantine, which can otherwise shrug off an Ivy Cudgel. At +2, Play Rough targets Dragon- and Fighting-types such as Kyurem, Kommo-o, and Iron Hands. After a Swords Dance boost, Superpower is great against Steel-types like Hisuian Goodra, Archaludon, and Ferrothorn; unboosted, it also OHKOes Kyurem after Stealth Rock chip. Taunt shuts down passive walls such as Toxapex, Gastrodon, and Thunder Wave Archaludon to force them out and get the opportunity to set up, while after a boost, Knock Off targets Sinistcha. Swampert provides entry hazard support to help Ogerpon-W wallbreak and pivoting with Flip Turn; its Electric immunity improves the matchup against the type, handling the likes of Zeraora, Iron Hands, and Regieleki. Empoleon and Pelipper remove hazards in Defog so that Ogerpon-W does not get worn down. Additionally, Empoleon threatens Fairy-types such as Tapu Lele and Alolan Ninetales, as well as Tornadus-T and Kyurem, while Pelipper sets up rain to boost Ogerpon-W's Ivy Cudgel, handles Grass-types like Meowscarada and Mega Venusaur, and brings it in safely with U-turn. In return, Empoleon appreciates Ogerpon-W handling Ground-types such as Great Tusk and the Landorus formes, while Pelipper appreciates the removal of Hisuian Arcanine, the Landorus formes, and Gholdengo. Choice Scarf Tapu Fini, with its amazing bulk, handles fast Fighting- and Dragon-types like Iron Valiant, Mega Lopunny, and Dragon Dance Roaring Moon and can shift its Choice Scarf to walls like Toxapex and Clodsire with Trick so Ogerpon-W can handle them more easily. Choice Specs Greninja, with its colorful coverage boosted by Protean, handles a multitude of threats like opposing Ogerpon-W, Tapu Bulu, and Mega Venusaur. When paired with Pelipper, Ogerpon-W's wallbreaking opens up the door for rain-boosted sweepers and cleaners such as Mega Swampert and Barraskewda.

movesets.name: Swords Dance (Grass)
movesets.description: This is the sample set before we work on new analyses. This will be updated as the metagame continues to develop. Stay tuned!

movesets.name: Utility Attacker
movesets.description: • The given EV spread allows Ogerpon-W to OHKO Tapu Fini with Wood Hammer and outspeed Landorus, allocating the remaining EVs to HP.
